subject: SLA template: availability envelope & latency carveouts for batched inference
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@stratify.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-07-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: SLA ask: availability & latency for batch-heavy model endpoints

Hi Karthik / Ben,

Thanks for the product walkthrough yesterday — the demos looked great. As we kick off procurement, we wanted to raise two SLA items that are must-haves for our compliance team before we can sign:

1) Availability baseline: we need clarity on the availability % that will be contractually guaranteed for the hosted endpoints used in production. Given our customer commitments, Stratify is targeting 99.99% if possible.

2) Latency SLO + batch carveout: most of our traffic is batched inference (business-hour, heavy tails). We understand batching can affect per-request latency during peak windows. We need explicit carveouts that: (a) allow higher latency thresholds for opt-in batched endpoints, and (b) define how those carveouts impact monthly service credit calculations.

Procurement also wants a monthly cap on credits (we propose 20% of monthly invoice) and clear definitions for scheduled maintenance (we need maintenance windows to be communicated 7 days in advance).

Can you share a short redline-friendly SLA template that shows availability %, remedy tiers, and a batched-inference exception section? We're trying to close by end of month.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Head of Platform Ops | Stratify.ai
Procurement: procure@stratify.ai

Team — forwarding Stratify's ask. Quick thoughts before I prepare the redline draft for Elena:

- Availability baseline: 99.95% is our standard hosted SLA. 99.99% is achievable only for Dedicated / Reserved capacity with operational commitments. We should offer a dual-path: 99.95% for hosted, and 99.99% as an upsell for Dedicated (with a minimum commitment).

- Remedy tiers (proposal):
  * Availability >= 99.95%: no credit
  * 99.90% <= Availability < 99.95%: 10% service credit of monthly invoice
  * 99.00% <= Availability < 99.90%: 30% service credit
  * Availability < 99.00%: 50% service credit (cap at X months)

- Monthly cap: recommend max 30% of monthly invoice for hosted; we can offer 10% cap for Dedicated customers.

- Maintenance: standard carveout of scheduled maintenance up to 8 hours per month (published 7 days out). For anything beyond, count it toward availability calculation.

- Batched-inference carveout: create a specific section that (a) requires customers to opt-in endpoints as "batched" in Console, (b) allows relaxed latency SLOs for those endpoints, and (c) excludes those opt-in endpoints from per-request latency remedies but still counts them in availability math.

I can draft a redline that includes a short "Batched Inference Exception" and a separate table with remedy caps by plan. Attaching a working draft and a short spreadsheet with credit math. Please highlight any commercial/legal blockers.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Karthik — thanks for the outline. A couple constraints from pricing/legal to keep in the redline:

1) Credit caps: our standard hosted cap historically sits at 30% of the monthly invoice; legal prefers a per-calendar-month cumulative cap (not rolling). We should avoid open-ended caps for hosted. 10% for Dedicated seems reasonable.

2) Maintenance notice: 7 days is fine for planned maintenance. For emergency maintenance that affects availability we need an internal escalation clause and a requirement to provide a post-incident report — that reduces risk for the customer without increasing credit exposure.

3) Batched endpoints: I like the opt-in idea. Important to note the customer's responsibility to mark endpoints correctly and to keep traffic patterns documented. Also propose a small fee differential (batched endpoints are charged per-batch compute units) — that reduces moral hazard where customers classify everything as "batched" to avoid latency SLAs.

4) Remedy tiers: swap the 10% and 30% bands to be a bit tighter around 99.9% to protect our tail. Suggest: 99.95 baseline; 99.90–99.95 => 8% credit; 99.00–99.90 => 25%; <99.00 => 50%; cap at 3x monthly invoice for remedy payout.

I'll mark up the draft PDF with these points and return.

Ben Carter
Sr. Director, Commercial Operations — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Couple of product/ops edits to keep the template accurate for Stratify's workload: 

- For Dedicated customers (which Stratify is evaluating), we can offer 99.98% if they commit to a 12-month reserved pool and agreed scaling controls (burst windows, scheduled retrain blackout). That should get them closer to the 99.99 they asked for.

- Latency: define p50/p95/p99 buckets and make clear the remedy only applies to p95 for interactive endpoints. Batched endpoints opt-in will have latency targets expressed as a per-batch completion window (e.g., 5 minutes) and will be excluded from per-request latency credits.

- Scheduled maintenance: propose a maximum 6-hour per-month scheduled maintenance carveout (we can do 8 but Ops prefers 6 — keeps MTTR discipline). We publish maintenance calendar in Console and send an in-product banner 7 days prior.

- Fallbacks: add an automated fallback policy clause (we keep a compatible smaller model variant that can be routed to during capacity constraints). If customer enables fallback, availability math should consider successful fallback responses as 'served' for availability calculations.

I updated the attached SLA draft (see SLA_Redwood_Stratifly_Draft_v1.pdf) and added a short spreadsheet for the credit math. If you agree, Karthik, I'll send to Elena with a cover note asking them to indicate whether they prefer Hosted vs Dedicated path.

Marissa Cole
Principal Product Manager — Redwood Inference

Elena — thanks again for the clarity on requirements. We prepared a redline-friendly SLA attachment that addresses the availability envelope, monthly remedy tiers, and a specific "Batched Inference Exception" section that you can opt into. High-level summary below: 

- Hosted path: 99.95% availability baseline. Remedy tiers: 99.90–99.95 => 8% credit; 99.00–99.90 => 25% credit; <99.00 => 50% credit (per-calendar-month cap at 3x monthly invoice). Max monthly credit cap: 30% of monthly invoice.

- Dedicated path: 99.98% (with 12-month reservation + operational commitments). Credited cap reduced to 10% of monthly invoice.

- Scheduled maintenance carveout: up to 6 hours scheduled maintenance per calendar month (7 days notice via Console and email). Emergency maintenance still counts against availability but will require a post-incident report within 5 business days.

- Batched Inference Exception:
  * Customer must opt-in endpoints in Console as 'batched'.
  * Batched endpoints have per-batch completion windows (default 5 minutes) and are excluded from per-request latency remedies.
  * Batched endpoints still count towards availability calculation (i.e., if service cannot accept queued batches due to an outage, that counts as unavailable).
  * Customers using batched endpoints will be billed on batch compute units (small rate differential).

- Fallbacks & mitigation: If fallback to a compatible model variant is enabled and returns a successful response within configured fallback windows, that request is treated as served for availability calculations.

Attached: SLA_Redwood_Stratifly_Draft_v1.pdf and SLA_exceptions_table.xlsx (credit math). Please review and let us know: (1) whether you prefer Hosted or Dedicated path, and (2) any requested redlines on the batched carveout or monthly cap. If we get confirmation, we'll circulate a DocuSign-ready doc and legal will follow up with final language.

Best,
